notes: Hand-written. Speeds and memory are order-of-magnitude estimates for ~1600 px images and 2-4k keypoints (Apple M-series = M2/M3 Pro-class via PyTorch MPS; CUDA = RTX 4090 / A100-class). The Mac app should prefer measured numbers from benchmark.json when present.

Licence information was compiled from memory of the upstream repositories and model hubs, not re-verified online. Entries with licence.uncertain = true MUST be checked before any commercial use. 'commercialUse' is a simplified reading, not legal advice.
Training-data licences (MegaDepth, ScanNet, CO3D, Habitat, ...) can add restrictions to weights beyond the code licence.

colmap_sift.summary: Classic SIFT features + nearest-neighbour matching inside COLMAP, followed by GLOMAP (global) or COLMAP (incremental) mapping.
strengths: Very accurate on well-textured, well-overlapping photos
weaknesses: Struggles with low texture, strong lighting changes and wide baselines
No GPU SIFT on macOS (CPU only), so slow for large sets
Exhaustive matching is quadratic
colmap_sift.bestFor: General photo and video captures with good texture; the safe default and the baseline every other model is compared against.

speed.appleSilicon: ~0.3-1 s/image extraction (CPU, multithreaded); ~10-40 ms/pair CPU matching
speed.notes: Mapping time (GLOMAP) is usually seconds to minutes; COLMAP incremental can take much longer on >500 images.

installSize.packages: ~150-400 MB (brew install colmap glomap pulls Ceres, CGAL, Qt...)

colmap_sift.install: brew install colmap glomap   |   Linux: apt install colmap (CPU) or build with CUDA

sift_lightglue.summary: SIFT keypoints matched by the LightGlue transformer instead of ratio-test nearest neighbours.
strengths: Much better matching than ratio test at wide baselines
weaknesses: SIFT detector still weak on low texture
Needs PyTorch
sift_lightglue.bestFor: A permissively-licensed upgrade over COLMAP SIFT for commercial use.

licence.notes: SIFT extraction via OpenCV (Apache-2.0) or pycolmap (BSD-3).

installSize.packages: PyTorch ~300 MB (macOS) / ~2.5-4 GB (Linux CUDA wheels) + lightglue/kornia ~10 MB

superpoint_lightglue.summary: Learned SuperPoint keypoints with the LightGlue matcher; the de-facto modern default for SfM in hloc pipelines.
strengths: Robust to illumination change and moderate viewpoint change
Fast on GPU, adaptive early-exit matching
Excellent registration rates on typical captures
weaknesses: NON-COMMERCIAL licence (SuperPoint weights)
Not rotation invariant (fails on in-plane rotated images)
Keypoints less precise than SIFT at sub-pixel level
superpoint_lightglue.bestFor: Personal / research reconstructions where robustness matters most.

licence.weights: SuperPoint: Magic Leap 'academic or non-profit noncommercial research use only' licence; LightGlue-SuperPoint weights: Apache-2.0
licence.notes: The SuperPoint detector weights are the restricting component.

disk_lightglue.summary: DISK learned features (trained with reinforcement learning on MegaDepth) matched with LightGlue.
weaknesses: Heavier extractor (U-Net) than SuperPoint
Not rotation invariant
Slower on MPS
disk_lightglue.bestFor: Outdoor and architectural captures where a commercially usable learned matcher is needed.

licence.notes: Believed Apache-2.0; trained on MegaDepth whose imagery comes from Flickr. Verify before commercial use.

aliked_lightglue.summary: ALIKED lightweight learned keypoints with deformable descriptors, matched with LightGlue.
strengths: Better than SuperPoint under viewpoint change in many benchmarks
weaknesses: Uses deformable convolutions: not natively supported on MPS, falls back to CPU (PYTORCH_ENABLE_MPS_FALLBACK=1 is set by splatprep) so it is slow on Mac
Not rotation invariant
aliked_lightglue.bestFor: CUDA workers; a commercial-friendly alternative to SuperPoint.

licence.notes: Licence recalled from the upstream repo; verify.

loftr.summary: Transformer-based dense-to-sparse matcher (kornia, outdoor weights) that needs no keypoint detector.
strengths: Finds matches in low-texture and repetitive regions where detectors fail
weaknesses: Matches are pair-specific, so tracks are fragmented (keypoints are merged on a half-pixel grid)
Slow: every pair runs the full network; poor scaling to large sets
Fixed working resolution (≤840 px) limits precision
loftr.bestFor: Small sets (<100 images) of low-texture scenes (white walls, product shots).

mast3r.summary: 3D-grounded dense matching + sparse global alignment from Naver; reconstructs poses and dense points directly, even from 2-3 images.
strengths: Works with very few / very wide-baseline views
weaknesses: NON-COMMERCIAL (CC BY-NC-SA)
Heavy ViT-Large: slow and memory hungry, practical only for tens of images
Not pip-installable (clone the repo)
Pose accuracy below classic SfM on dense captures
mast3r.bestFor: Sparse captures (5-50 photos) where COLMAP fails to register.

installSize.packages: PyTorch + repo requirements (~200 MB, optional curope CUDA kernels)

mast3r.install: git clone --recursive https://github.com/naver/mast3r; pip install -r requirements; export SPLATPREP_MAST3R_PATH=...

vggt.summary: Visual Geometry Grounded Transformer (Meta, CVPR 2025): predicts cameras, depth and points for all frames in one forward pass.
strengths: Seconds for tens of frames on a GPU
Robust on sparse and low-texture inputs
weaknesses: 1B parameters: high memory, grows with frame count
No bundle adjustment here, so poses are less precise than SfM for splat training
Licence of the original checkpoint is non-commercial (see note)
Works at 518 px internally
vggt.bestFor: Quick previews and sparse captures (<150 frames) on a CUDA worker.

speed.appleSilicon: ~10-60 s for 20-50 frames (MPS, fp32), if memory allows
speed.cuda: ~0.2 s for 10 frames, ~3 s for 100 frames (H100-class)

licence.weights: facebook/VGGT-1B: non-commercial; facebook/VGGT-1B-Commercial: commercial use permitted after access approval (set SPLATPREP_VGGT_WEIGHTS)
licence.notes: Recalled from the 2025 release notes; the exact terms of both checkpoints must be verified.

opencv_sift.summary: Dependency-light baseline: OpenCV RootSIFT + ratio test + mutual check, verified with MAGSAC++. Needs pycolmap or COLMAP for full SfM, otherwise matching-only.
weaknesses: CPU only
Ratio-test matching is weaker than LightGlue
Brute-force matching cost grows with keypoints
opencv_sift.bestFor: Testing the pipeline and machines without PyTorch.

person.summary: DeepLabV3-MobileNetV3 (torchvision) segments people; masks keep everything except (dilated) people.
weaknesses: Coarse boundaries
Misses tiny / heavily occluded people
Does not handle other transients (cars, pets)
person.bestFor: Outdoor/public captures with people walking through.

licence.weights: torchvision pretrained weights (COCO subset, VOC classes)
licence.notes: COCO annotations are CC BY 4.0; images follow Flickr terms. Verify.

sky.summary: SegFormer-B0 (ADE20K 'sky') via transformers when installed, else a dependency-free heuristic (bright/blue/smooth region connected to the top border). Keeps everything except sky.
strengths: Stops the trainer from placing floaters in the sky
weaknesses: Heuristic fails on overcast/white skies touching white buildings
SegFormer weights are non-commercial
sky.bestFor: Outdoor scenes with large sky regions.

licence.weights: NVIDIA SegFormer: NVIDIA Source Code License (non-commercial research)
licence.notes: Swap SPLATPREP_SKY_MODEL for a commercially licensed segmenter if needed.

sam2_auto.summary: Segment Anything 2. Without maskPrompts: object-centric (object chosen automatically or from a first-frame maskPrompt, kept as 255, propagated with the video predictor). With maskPrompts (Mac mask editor): the clicked objects are tracked forward and backward and removed (0), same as sam2_track.
weaknesses: Propagation drifts on unordered photo sets (works best on video-like sequences)
Auto-prompt can pick the wrong object; use maskPrompt / maskPrompts
sam2_auto.bestFor: Object-centric captures (products, sculptures) to cut away the background.

memory.appleSilicon: 2-4 GB unified (chunked: bounded by maskChunkSize, not by frame count)

sam2_track.summary: Removes the objects you click or box on ANY frame (maskPrompts): each is tracked forward and backward through the whole sequence with the SAM 2 video predictor (chunked, so 500+ frames fit in memory). Pairs with the maskserver for instant single-frame previews.
strengths: Exact control: masks precisely what the user selected
Prompts on several frames refine the same object
weaknesses: Needs user interaction
Tracking can drift or lose objects after long occlusions or on unordered photo sets (add another prompt on a later frame)
Cost grows with objects x frames (two sweeps)
sam2_track.bestFor: Removing specific transient things (a passer-by, a pet, a parked car that moved) the automatic detector missed or got wrong.

speed.appleSilicon: ~0.2-0.5 s per object-frame (hiera-small, MPS); preview ~0.5-1 s new image, <0.1 s re-click

dynamic.summary: Open-vocabulary detection of transient classes (people, pets, vehicles, bikes, strollers, umbrellas, bags... configurable via maskClasses) on every frame with OWLv2, then SAM 2 segments and tracks every detected instance through the ordered sequence (fills detector misses, re-prompted when new detections appear). Objects are dilated and set to 0 so they are ignored in training. Unordered photo sets use SAM 2 per image.
strengths: Any class by name, no retraining
SAM 2 tracking fills frames where the detector missed
Pixel-accurate boundaries + dilation margin for shadows/motion blur
weaknesses: Masks every instance of a listed class, moving or not (a parked car or a sleeping cat is removed too)
OWLv2 confidence is low/uncalibrated: 'bag' and 'umbrella' give false positives on clutter; tune maskThreshold / maskClasses
Slowest mask model (detector on every frame + SAM 2 per object-frame)
Shadows and reflections of objects are not detected
dynamic.bestFor: Captures with people, pets or traffic moving through the scene.

speed.appleSilicon: ~0.6 s/frame detection (OWLv2-base, MPS) + ~0.2-0.5 s per object-frame SAM 2 tracking

memory.appleSilicon: 3-5 GB unified (detector is freed before SAM 2 loads)

licence.notes: OWLv2 weights trained on WebLI pseudo-labels + LVIS/Objects365; licence as published on the Hugging Face model card.
